title: $27,092 on paper, down from $98,828 in mid-October. Same AI-laggard call bot, 264 trades. At what point would you have switched it off?
author: QuanTradin
selftext:
Paper money, simulated, not advice. This card comes off one of the house paper bots on Quantradin, an app I built myself.

The rule in one line: watch a basket of AI names that usually move together, and when one lags the group, buy a daily call on the laggard and wait for it to catch up.

| | |
|---|---|
| Period | 25 Aug to 9 Nov |
| Trades | 264 |
| Trades that won | 35.6% |
| Realized | +$27,091.51 |
| Best streak | 12 in a row |

The total isn't why I'm posting it. Look at the curve. Flat for most of September, one steep climb into October, and when I first shared this bot on Oct 20 its card read +$98,828. Since then it has handed back roughly 70% of that, a little at a time, with no single bad day you could point to.

That's the part I keep going back and forth on. Nothing broke. The rule fires the same way it always did. AI names stopped moving as one group, so "the laggard catches up" stopped being true often enough to pay for the calls, and every losing call costs the whole premium.

Saw the thread here today about three models on paper accounts where most pattern ideas died at a random-entry comparison. That's the check I haven't run on this one yet: same rule, but buy a random member of the basket instead of the laggard. If the random version made the same climb in October, the money came from the AI run, not from picking the laggard, and the slide is just the run ending.

How Quantradin helps here: you, or an AI you connect (Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, Codex...), write out the trade in everyday words and it gets tested on past US stock and option prices with no look-ahead, option fills at the bid and ask instead of the middle, and whatever survives keeps running as a paper bot, so a slide like this one shows up on paper first. Free, paper only. [quantradin.com](http://quantradin.com)

So where would your line have been? A fixed drawdown from the peak, a number of losing weeks, or the moment the basket stopped moving together?

comments.author: dn4r
comments.body:
What the chart's actually saying....
The whole P&L came from one burst. It sat flat for about a month, ripped for roughly two weeks from late September to mid-October, then slowly bled out. It's given back $71.7k, which is 72.6% of the peak.

The 12-win streak isn't something to brag about. It's a warning sign. With a 35.6% win rate, the odds of 12 straight wins across 264 independent trades are about 1 in 1,500. It happened because the trades aren't independent. When the basket catches up, it catches up all at once, so one good day turns into a dozen "wins." So 264 trades is really just a few separate bets.

The card shows +$27k but leaves out max drawdown.....
And "real fills" on paper trades in daily single-stock options is pretty generous. Live slippage across 264 trades would take a real chunk out of that which is why paper trading is usually horse shit.

No order slippage, no fees, no draw down, ran when the market had a rally, you have no kill switch in place.

Sorry for sounding brutal....

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: fair hit. the clustering I'd missed completely: 12 straight wins at that rate means the trades moved together, so 264 trades is really a few bets. options here fill on the far side of the spread, never the middle, but no fees are charged, and max drawdown belongs on the card.

comments.author: dn4r
comments.body:
fair enough on the fills, buying the ask and selling the bid is harsher than most paper setups. id still put fees in tho. on 30c dailies youre paying like 4% of premium every round trip at normal commissions and that stacks up quick over 264 trades

id also score it on daily pnl instead of per trade. if the wins come in bunches the win rate and streak dont really tell you much. max dd, worst day and how long since a new high would answer your own question straight off the card

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: both fair. the card charges no fees at all, so on 30c dailies the real line sits below what it shows, and 4% a round trip over 264 trades adds up. daily P&L with max drawdown and days since a new high would have told the burst story without anyone squinting at the chart. I built Quantradin and the card is its export, so that goes on my list.
